whatItIs.text: Unopened flower buds of a spiny Mediterranean shrub, pickled or salt-cured — tiny bursts of brine that cut through rich food.

historyNote.text: The caper bush grows all around the Mediterranean (its original home is debated); the buds and the larger caper berries are eaten salted or pickled, and the plant's other parts go into medicines and cosmetics.

howToChoose.text: Choose brine-packed capers with small, even buds (smaller means more delicate); salt-packed taste rounder but need rinsing.

storage.text: Keep the jar sealed in the fridge after opening, with buds under brine.

foodSafetyRef.note: Practice storage guidance only; no rulebook content is claimed. The app's food-safety rules live in data/food-safety/rules.json.

useItUp.text: Fry capers crisp in butter for pasta or fish, mash into butter for bread, or chop into vinaigrettes and tapenades — they are best in small, frequent doses.

substitutions.note: saltier and oilier; rinse if very briny
